title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) that tested whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used paired evaluation (Npairs=200), generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate consumed by both conditions), declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes), model_calls_used=200, and repair calls invoked=0. Outcome: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar two‑sided p=1.00). The null result is design‑bound: because a single shared candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every case, the guarded repair stage was never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and interpret the run‑level null result as a ceiling effect caused by the preregistered shared generation semantics and high oracle coverage. We provide artifact‑anchored recommendations for informative future comparisons (independent sampling, calibrated task difficulty, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests).

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent→configuration agents for network operations. A central operational risk is misconfiguration: syntactically plausible but operationally incorrect outputs that violate ordering, safety, or vendor idioms. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→repair where a generator proposes a configuration, a deterministic validator (oracle) checks objective properties (reachability, protected interfaces, transition safety), and a repair module iteratively remedies detected violations. Prior system work (constraint‑based adaptation, validator‑augmented agents) reports improved reliability in practice, but quantitative, preregistered, fully archived comparisons remain rare. We preregistered a paired, confirmatory emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to test whether verifier‑assistance yields higher oracle pass rates than unconstrained generation under a tightly specified experimental plan. The preregistration froze the generation semantics to shared_initial_candidate (one generator call per pair) and limited repairs to ≤1 call/task; these design choices are central to the outcome reported here. Our contribution is an artifact‑anchored report of the preregistered run, a deterministic accounting of why the guarded repair stage was never invoked, and concrete reproducible recommendations—grounded in archived artifacts and hashes—on how to design informative follow‑ups.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps covers intent translation, configuration synthesis, RAG grounding, and verifier/constraint augmentation. Benchmarks such as NetConfEval evaluate translation accuracy; systems like MeshAgent and LLM‑NetCFG encode invariants and validators to improve safety; verifier‑grounded repair workflows (e.g., StruSpec) demonstrate verifier‑driven improvements in program/DSL domains. Our experiment differs by preregistering the estimand, generation semantics, validator, and analysis executor, then executing an autonomous, fully archived run whose raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are all hashed and preserved. Representative verified sources used to position this work (MeshAgent, NetConfEval, StruSpec) are included in the supplied evidence bundle and cited accordingly.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental design (artifact): We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 (SHA‑256: a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Design: paired binary evaluation with Npairs=200 (planned episodes=400). Task bank: four protocol buckets (BGP, OSPF, ACL, VLAN) of 50 pairs each; per protocol vendor allocation: Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (totals Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64). Complexity: per protocol 25 simple and 25 complex (simple total=100, complex total=100). Model and adapter: declared model gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model configuration archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate — a single generator call per pair produced one candidate provided to both baseline and guarded conditions. Validator and repair: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored every candidate; repair budget ≤1 call/task (repair not invoked in this run). Analysis: paired_binary_analysis_v1 using paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Missingness policy: primary analysis requires complete pairs; provider/infrastructure failures would be excluded and logged. Reproducibility measures: every prompt, raw output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record and analysis artifact was archived and SHA‑256 hashed (execution/execution_manifest.json contains per‑file digests and paths).
sections.results: Execution and scoring (artifact‑backed): the run completed per the preregistered plan: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs). Scoring summary (artifact: analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951): baseline_success_count=200/200 (100%); guarded_success_count=200/200 (100%). Contingency (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) is fully concordant: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory analysis (artifact: analysis/results.json) yielded paired difference = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10,000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. Deterministic reconciliation (artifact: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirms accounting consistency across provider calls, raw responses, scoring files and analysis artifacts. Representative scoring and validator traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b) show parsed command counts, normalized configurations, validator decision fields (valid=true), and repair_applied=false. Provider call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count=200; cache_hit_count=0; cache_miss_count=200 (execution manifest entries and per‑call provider traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/; full per‑file hashes are recorded).
sections.discussion: Causal account and ceiling effect: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one generated candidate per pair that both conditions consumed. In this run every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle; consequently the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0) and no measurable guarded benefit could materialize. The observed null result is therefore a design‑bound ceiling effect, not evidence that verifier‑assistance is ineffectual in general. Statistical interpretation: perfect concordance (n11=200) yields zero empirical variance of the paired difference; the bootstrap CI and exact test reflect that degenerate outcome (CI=[0.00,0.00], McNemar p=1.00). This is an artifact of the frozen generation semantics and the validator's acceptance region given the provided task bank and generator behavior. Practical recommendations (artifact‑grounded): (1) independent generation semantics — draw an independent generator candidate per condition to allow generator variance to create failing candidates and permit repairs to act; (2) task difficulty calibration — augment the task bank with higher adversarial or boundary tasks so initial generator candidates sometimes fail the oracle (artifact: execution/task_manifest.jsonl can be extended and rerun); (3) larger repair budgets and iterative repair — allow multiple repair iterations per task and richer repair prompts so the repair module can demonstrate improvement; (4) validator stress tests and oracle coverage diagnostics — vary validator strictness and log oracle_coverage_ambiguous flags to reveal blind spots (analysis/contamination_summary.csv and analysis/contamination_summary artifacts are included); (5) multi‑model replication — execute the same pipeline across multiple models and adapters to assess generality. Reproducibility and auditability: all artifacts needed to reproduce or rerun alternate variants are archived and hashed, including execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/responses/, execution/provider_calls/, execution/scoring/, analysis/*, execution/model_configuration.json, and the preregistration artifact (SHA‑256s are in the bundle).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an auditable paired emulation run to measure verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair effectiveness under frozen shared_initial_candidate semantics. Both baseline and guarded conditions achieved 200/200 oracle passes, repair was never invoked, and the paired difference was 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.00). The null result is explained by a preregistered design choice (shared initial generation) that created a ceiling effect: a single shared candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task and therefore prevented repair from being exercised. We publish the full artifact bundle (prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest, analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑anchored guidance for informative future experiments (independent sampling, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets, and validator stress tests). The archived materials permit direct reproducible reruns and controlled extensions that will determine whether verifier‑assistance reduces misconfiguration under experimental regimes where repair can act.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact‑backed):

This master prompt launched the autonomous post‑lock research run. The Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the master prompt pre‑lock; all substantive research actions reported here were performed autonomously after the lock.
- Preregistration (frozen): study id = study-cnd-2026-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2. The preregistration froze the primary hypothesis, sampling plan, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, validator, repair budget, stopping rules, and analysis executor.
- LLM and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini used via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). All provider call traces and raw responses are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate per pair and provided to both baseline and guarded conditions). This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs) and is the proximate cause the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0). The execution manifest records these counts and per‑file hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored every candidate; representative scoring artifact: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b). All validator traces are archived and hashed.
- Repair policy and budgeting: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; in this run repair calls invoked = 0 (artifact‑backed). Repair prompts would have been archived if used.
- Analysis procedures (frozen): paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples (seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Confirmatory analysis artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).
- Execution and reproducibility: every prompt, model output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record, manifest and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 digests. Deterministic reconciliation confirms arithmetic and accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256 = 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174).
- Human involvement: pre‑lock collaborative development and approval of the master prompt were performed by the Research Director. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations: none affecting the primary confirmatory analysis; model identifier did not change mid‑run; no pairs excluded; repair stage not triggered. Full execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are included in the artifact bundle for audit.
limitations: Confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200).

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0), preventing measurable guarded benefit in this run.
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor images, runtime nondeterminism, device‑specific quirks).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (uncovered semantic failure modes) remain possible; oracle‑coverage diagnostics are archived and annotated in the artifact bundle.
